steps.title: Lesson 2: Core Concepts
steps.body: Key Fact: The League of Nations was created as part of the Treaty of Versailles in June 1919. It was Woodrow Wilson's idea - his Fourteenth Point called for "a general association of nations." The League's headquarters were in Geneva, Switzerland. Its first meeting was held on 15 November 1920 with 42 member states. | Key Fact: The League's Covenant (its founding document) set out its key principles: collective security, arbitration of disputes, disarmament, and improved living and working conditions worldwide. Article 10 of the Covenant committed all members to "respect and preserve" each other's territorial integrity. | Key Fact: The Council was the most powerful body.
